sections.title: Executive Verdict
paragraphs: Mother Nutri Foods is a small B2B peanut-butter and roasted-peanut manufacturer, not an established branded-food compounder. Reported revenue and operating profit are growing, but the expansion has absorbed substantial working capital. Customer concentration, repeated bank-versus-book discrepancies and IPO deposits pledged against borrowings outweigh the headline FY26 revenue increase of 36.6%. [E02–E15]

Conclusion: Hold—unresolved. This is a speculative expansion or special-situation thesis. Diagnostic BQS is 4.2 and GQS is capped at 5.0; both are excluded from rankings because the financial-reliability gate is material. IAS is NS. ₹155 is only an assumed scenario price, not a verified 19 October close. No ordinary buy range or expected return is supportable. Corrected disclosures, demonstrated cash collection, genuinely funded expansion and authenticated trading history could reopen the case.

sections.title: Business Overview
paragraphs: The company buys peanuts, manufactures and packages peanut butter, and supplies roasted peanuts largely to B2B and private-label customers. Its Mahuva facility in Gujarat benefits from proximity to input supply and export logistics. Revenue recognition on product delivery/control transfer is separate from customer collection. No enforceable recurring-revenue contract base or quantified order book was established. [E03–E06]

Peanut-butter revenue declined from ₹75.5420 crore in FY23 to ₹66.4661 crore in FY24 and ₹62.2006 crore in FY25. Roasted-peanut revenue expanded from ₹0.0550 crore to ₹27.2179 crore. The own brand, Spread & Eat, contributed only 1.52% of FY25 sales. The H1 FY26 mix was 60.13% peanut butter and 39.55% roasted peanuts. A FY26 product split was not found, so the report does not invent one.

Exports fell from ₹31.3716 crore to ₹26.9614 crore in FY26 while total revenue reached ₹123.2782 crore. Domestic sales drove the aggregate increase. Earlier UK and South Africa sales also rotated materially, making a simple export-growth narrative unreliable. Product mix, input prices and foreign exchange complicate a pure volume interpretation.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
paragraphs: Quality systems, aflatoxin testing, customization and timely private-label delivery can support repeat business. They are useful capabilities, but also common requirements for participation in food supply. The prospectus reports a repeat-customer percentage of 41.03% in FY25 and 76.92% in H1 FY26. It does not demonstrate a sustained price premium or contractual switching barrier. One strong half-year does not establish a moat. [E03–E05]

The top two customers generated 52.30% of FY25 sales and the top ten 91.73%. The largest supplier represented 36.24% of purchases and the top ten 80.75%. Large private-label buyers can renegotiate prices or move sourcing. Agricultural input shocks, quality rejection, recall exposure and customer credit are linked risks. A 1.52% own-brand share is not a basis for branded-FMCG economics.

Comparators establish boundaries rather than a valuation target. ADF Foods has established ethnic-food brands, international distribution and a stronger funding profile. AVT Natural supplies plant-based extracts and ingredients. Prataap Snacks is a consumer-snack brand business. None is a clean peer for this peanut-butter/private-label mix. No dated peer multiple is transplanted. Better retention, normalized price realization and persistent incremental returns would be needed for a moat upgrade. [E22]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
paragraphs: Revenue increased from ₹75.9396 crore in FY23 to ₹123.2782 crore in FY26, a three-year CAGR of 17.527%. Absolute additions in FY24, FY25 and FY26 were ₹4.9764 crore, ₹9.3271 crore and ₹33.0351 crore. The three-year period is the longest coherent corporate operating history available. Five- and ten-year CAGRs are NS; predecessor figures are not spliced in. The framework maps 17.53% to REV 7, with no trajectory bonus. [E02]

The April 2022 business transfer distorts FY23 acquisition-related cash flow. No subsequent acquisition was identified, so FY24–26 growth is organic at the entity level. The split between price, volume and mix is not fully disclosed. Declining peanut-butter revenue and growing roasted-peanut sales provide an economic cross-check. FY26 export contraction means the growth is not broad-based across channels.

Capacity was 8,000 MTPA. FY23–25 production of 4,412.35, 5,097.59 and 5,685.48 MT implies utilization of 55.15%, 63.72% and 71.07%. H1 FY26 production of 3,793 MT against half-year capacity of 4,000 MT implies 94.83% utilization for that period. This is not a full-year output forecast. The proposed 15,200 MTPA total capacity is not verified as commissioned at the cutoff.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
paragraphs: Private-label food and roasted peanuts offer a plausible growth route, but access depends on anchor customers, product quality, capacity completion and collections. The ₹23.1934 crore proposed plant adds 7,200 MTPA; a capacity plan alone does not prove orders or returns. Working capital, rather than existing fixed assets, has absorbed most recent incremental capital. [E04,E05,E14,E20]

The funded-capital proxy rises from ₹35.5400 crore in FY24 to ₹83.4594 crore in FY26 after excluding cash and term deposits. NOPAT at a normalized 25% tax rate rises from ₹5.8578 crore to ₹11.5092 crore. The incremental return is 11.7936%, below an analyst cost-of-capital range of 13–16%. Using the 17.16% rate disclosed in the IPO tax reconciliation gives 13.0264%, still not strong excess-return evidence. The actual FY26 effective tax rate is different: 17.9453%.

The proxy retains unidentified advances as capital committed. It is not a precise asset-side operating-capital measure or a project IRR. No later acquisition or revaluation explains the FY24–26 bridge, so a bounded CAP score is possible without private project cohorts. CAP is 4. Raw GQS of 5.35 is capped at 5.0 because cash realization is persistently weak. Retaining all pledged deposits within committed capital raises incremental capital to ₹71.5604 crore and lowers the return to about 7.90%. This collateral-inclusive sensitivity reinforces weak incremental economics rather than treating restricted IPO money as idle free capital.

Deposits of ₹23.7623 crore secure SBI overdrafts of ₹20.8208 crore. A full paired unwind leaves only ₹2.9415 crore: ₹2.3726 crore of net plant-earmarked funding plus at most ₹0.5689 crore of non-IPO residual, subject to release. It cannot release the full ₹23.1934 crore plant allocation while leaving the OD outstanding. Remaining GCP/fee proceeds of ₹1.4383 crore were already credited to HDFC CC and cannot be counted again. No prospective issue or promoter promise is treated as received money.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
paragraphs: Founder-family experience and operating growth are positives. Gross promoter borrowings were ₹23.5578 crore and repayments ₹24.4418 crore, against an opening ₹0.8840 crore balance, leaving zero. Sigma Cold advances of ₹13.9333 crore came in and went out, also leaving zero. Large gross related-party transactions warrant scrutiny of terms; they are not proof of diversion. Remuneration was not identified as excessive relative to profit. Reimbursements and the ₹0.6007 crore promoter expense receivable still require clear purpose and settlement. [E17]

Promoters held 65.93% at March 2026. IPO OFS proceeds belong to sellers; fresh-issue proceeds belong to the company. The new plant land is leased from a promoter for 15 years. A reliable future rent schedule was not found. The model retains recurring rent within its assumed EBIT margin and does not add lease/property value separately. The annual report’s no-leasing statement and prospectus land lease need clarification, rather than an assumption that rent is zero.

The original plan expected ₹7.4109 crore of FY26 plant spending, ₹15.7826 crore in FY27 and commercial production in September 2026. The March 2026 utilization certificate shows zero plant spending. That is verified early slippage. Without a later completion filing, October commissioning is unknown, not proven to have failed. Existing operations nevertheless grew strongly. EXEC 4 balances those facts. [E05]

Repeated bank-versus-book differences and stale audit language matter more than small, regularized statutory late fees. G1 is Conditional, not Fail, because material misconduct has not been established. G2 is Hold because unresolved reliability questions affect inventory, receivables and funding capacity.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
paragraphs: FY26 revenue of ₹123.2782 crore produces PBT of ₹14.1842 crore and PAT of ₹11.6388 crore. Removing other income of ₹1.1016 crore and adding finance cost of ₹2.2630 crore gives operating EBIT of ₹15.3456 crore. Adding D&A of ₹0.4887 crore gives EBITDA of ₹15.8343 crore. Other income includes interest and FX; reported profit growth is not identical to operating growth. Weighted EPS of ₹11.09 is not the current-share EPS: PAT divided by 12,535,020 shares gives about ₹9.285. [E10,E18]

Reported FY26 CFO of minus ₹45.3950 crore includes a ₹23.6411 crore increase in term deposits. Reclassifying that investment gives minus ₹21.7539 crore. Subtract financing interest paid of ₹2.2630 crore to get minus ₹24.0169 crore after interest; subtract cash capex of ₹0.4250 crore for minus ₹24.4419 crore of owner-equivalent FCF. This is an analyst reclassification, not a replacement audited statement. FY24–26 adjusted CFO/PAT is minus 1.0967. FY23 is excluded because acquisition opening-balance treatment distorts cash-flow comparability. [E10,E11]

The gross provision/tax presentation reconciles exactly. The ₹1.3037 crore excess of reported provision movement over the balance-sheet change offsets the same excess of reported tax paid over current tax. A conventional bridge using non-tax provision movement of ₹0.0196 crore and tax cash of ₹1.4180 crore preserves CFO. This is not an unexplained net-cash discrepancy. [E13]

Receivables of ₹36.3922 crore are reported as less than six months from due date, with no doubtful provision. Inventory of ₹44.0808 crore includes substantial finished goods. Supplier advances of ₹3.4254 crore, GST receivable of ₹2.6292 crore, other loans/advances of ₹4.0218 crore and the ₹0.6007 crore promoter expense receivable tie up further capital. None is free cash. Payables fell from ₹20.9254 crore to ₹8.4691 crore, reducing supplier financing.

The complete statutory audit and annexure coverage is shown below. FY26 has an unmodified main opinion and an effective IFC opinion. CARO discloses bank-return differences but reports no default, fraud, wilful default or cash loss. The export-cutoff KAM does not itself establish overstatement. Audit-trail operation exceptions in FY24/FY25 and the stale FY25 date in the FY26 paragraph remain unresolved. FY23 says CARO/IFC reporting is exempt while an attached IFC note refers to 2016; that is not a contemporary control pass. [E07–E09]

MSME principal of ₹18.8255 crore in Note 32 conflicts with ₹5.5546 crore in the balance-sheet note, a ₹13.2709 crore gap. Base funding uses the balance sheet; a separate stress treats the gap as an incremental claim, rather than automatically double-counting it. The ₹1.2632 crore appealed tax demand, including interest, is contingent and paid in the bear stress. Debt, FD, old tax, statutory dues, gratuity, IPO fees and term principal are reconciled once. [E12–E16]

It does not establish a current listed-issuer default. However, the 2022 acquisition allocation included secured and unsecured loans, so it cannot simply be dismissed as an unrelated namesake. sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
paragraphs: There is no authenticated 19 October 2026 close. At an assumed ₹155 only, market capitalization is ₹194.2928 crore, current-share P/E is about 16.69× and EV/EBITDA about 14.87× without netting restricted deposits. The paired FD/OD settlement sensitivity retains the residual plant earmark; it does not simply subtract all deposits. Negative owner cash flow makes the earnings multiple alone unpersuasive. No matched peer valuation or assured execution is claimed.

The monthly model starts on 31 March 2026, splits at the 20 October entry and ends exactly on 20 October 2031. It pays existing tax, statutory dues, gratuity, remaining IPO fees and term principal across FY27. Interest follows the paired OD unwind, and new facility draw is limited to ₹0.4566 crore of documented sanction headroom. Continued CC rollover is conditional and separately stressed. Core ONWC starts at ₹77.7057 crore; non-operating advances and the promoter receivable are not assumed collected. The ₹0.25 crore operating reserve is an analyst choice, not a covenant.

Base assumptions are 12% revenue growth, 11.5% EBIT margin, 60% terminal ONWC/revenue, ₹23.1934 crore of project spending over FY27–28, 25% tax, 9% interest and 10× terminal EBITDA. Bear combines 2% growth, 7.5% margin, more working capital, a delayed project with 20% overrun and payment of the tax claim. Bull assumes 18% growth, 13.5% margin, 52% ONWC and 12× EBITDA. Maintenance capex of 1.5% of revenue continues. Sales beyond 1.9 times FY26 require extra capacity capex at 25% of incremental excess revenue. With no project, that capacity threshold remains the existing revenue base; no free new capacity is granted.

All three expansion paths breach the cash floor without new funds. Their non-rescue terminal prices, returns and entry values are therefore null. Each explicit rescue pre-funds the maximum deficit upfront with whole shares at an assumed ₹108.50, a 30% discount to the ₹155 scenario price, less 5% issue costs. This is hypothetical financing, not an actual or approved issue. Dilution means new shares divided by post-issue shares; share expansion uses original shares as denominator. No later top-ups or post-terminal funding are allowed.

Terminal equity is continuing-business EV less debt plus cash after retaining an operating reserve. Unused earmarks remain excluded, including in the deferral case. Property, inventory and receivables are not added again to earnings-based EV. A low-growth deferral branch can be funded subject to the same release and rollover conditions; a zero-growth deferral is also tested. This distinguishes a growth-financing gap from unavoidable insolvency. Ordinary returns remain null because the gates are unresolved.

Reverse expectations use a finite 0–60% growth scan in five-point steps, with endogenous rescue dilution and extra capacity investment. No verified crossing of the 15% hurdle is found. The 60% endpoint is not reported as required growth, and the bounded test is not proof that no mathematical solution exists under any assumptions. Full 12/15/18% hurdle, WC-by-capex and growth-by-multiple sensitivities follow. These are conditional diagnostics, not ordinary entry recommendations.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
paragraphs: The strongest bear case is not that demand for peanut butter disappears. It is that concentrated customers pay slowly while finished goods and advances rise, suppliers withdraw credit, pledged deposits cannot pay both the bank and the plant, and external capital arrives on dilutive terms. A commodity or food-quality shock can amplify the same cash constraint. [E04,E10,E14,E15]

The linked bear combines weak growth, lower margin, more working capital, project delay/overrun and the tax claim. Its explicit rescue produces a materially negative conditional return at ₹155; the unfunded path has no assigned return. Separate CC non-renewal and incremental MSME-claim tests quantify funding exposure without asserting those events have happened.

The counterargument is that FY26 growth temporarily loaded inventory and receivables, that supplier repayments front-loaded cash needs, and that collections and the IPO credit arrangement can normalize. Under-six-month debtor ageing, positive operating earnings and the unmodified audit support that possibility. It becomes investable only when receipts and reconciliations are evidenced. Persistent dependence on new capital to realize old reported profits would break the thesis; one weaker quarter would not.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
paragraphs: Neither 5× nor 10× is an evidence-backed base case. The exact five-year price CAGRs are about 38.0% and 58.5%, but percentages alone do not establish feasibility. At 12× terminal EBITDA and a 14.5% EBITDA margin, the table backsolves required sales, equity, working capital and extra capacity using the bull-rescue share count. It assumes no terminal surplus and ₹21 crore debt. Further funding would cause more dilution, so these are optimistic necessary conditions, not funded target prices.

Required sales and working capital would exceed the planned 15,200 MTPA footprint unless pricing, mix or additional facilities alter the economics. No order book, demonstrated market share or diversified customer base establishes that outcome. More capacity requires more capital rather than merely a higher terminal multiple. Reliability, funding and tradability holds remain binding.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
paragraphs: Final classification: Hold—unresolved. Business quality is mixed/speculative at an unrounded BQS of 4.18; GQS is capped at 5.00; IAS is NS. This is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate. GOV, MOAT, CAP, CASH, BAL and the unresolved gates fail the compounder criteria. Neither a proven-governance-failure label nor a current-default label is justified. Quality and investment rankings remain excluded.

Action category: research priority for reconciliation, not eligible for investment consideration. A cheaper quote alone cannot fix reliability or tradability. Reopen after corrected bank/MSME/control disclosures, current collection and funding evidence, documented commissioning and dated BSE trading history. Then rebuild the ordinary five-year return and 15% entry range using an authenticated price. An existing-holder decision would also require actual position size, execution constraints, taxes and concentration context.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
paragraphs: Company annual reports, full statutory audit annexures, the IPO prospectus and the utilization certificate control the analysis. Ratings are used with issuer and period checks. The official security master verifies identity and lot size. Sixty internally dated NSE files contain no issuer rows; absence is not zero BSE turnover. Three primary BSE quote/history requests returned 403. Rolling quote pages are not used to authenticate the cutoff close.

Historical versions are retained rather than silently blended. The main history uses FY23 IPO-restated figures, FY24 from the FY25 annual-report comparative and FY25/FY26 from the latest FY26 annual report. Alternative IPO-restated FY24/FY25 rows remain available. FY23 CFO is excluded from organic conversion. Comparative regroupings are disclosed without treating every change as an error. The capital calculation uses an explicit NOPAT and funded-capital definition, not reported ROCE alone.

Open questions are the granular bank reconciliation; corrected MSME balance; current audit-trail operation; legacy rating obligation mapping; actual post-March plant spending and commissioning; bank release and CC renewal; the promoter-land lease cash schedule; receipts of receivables and advances; FY26 product price/volume data; current promoter pledges; and dated BSE turnover, spread, circuit and surveillance information. These gaps affect the conclusion and are not filled with neutral assumptions.

summary: Mother Nutri Foods is a small B2B peanut-butter and roasted-peanut manufacturer, not an established branded-food compounder. Reported revenue and operating profit are growing, but the expansion has absorbed substantial working capital. Customer concentration, repeated bank-versus-book discrepancies and IPO deposits pledged against borrowings outweigh the headline FY26 revenue increase of 36.6%. [E02–E15]
